claim: Faster SMA systems work better than slower ones on volatile semiconductor assets
test: Sharpe(fast: SMA10/30, EMA12/26, SMA20/50) - Sharpe(slow: SMA50/200, >SMA200, monthly SMA210); compare the mean difference in semiconductors (C+D) with broad ETFs (A); Mann-Whitney p
evidence: Fast-slow Sharpe: semis mean -0.132 (n=14, 7% positive); broad mean -0.072 (n=7); difference -0.060; p=0.172

claim: SMA10/30 offers better downside protection than SMA20/50 but lags in rapidly reversing (sideways) markets
test: Across assets: max-drawdown difference (10/30 minus 20/50, positive = shallower) and sideways-regime excess return difference; sign tests
evidence: Drawdown shallower for 10/30 on 53% of 32 assets (median +0.013, p=0.860); sideways-regime excess return lower for 10/30 on 47% (median +0.186%/yr, p=0.860); Sharpe higher for 10/30 on 44%

claim: Faster exits and slower re-entries improve risk-adjusted returns by limiting drawdowns
test: Pairs differing only in re-entry speed: F02_02 (re-enter >SMA50) vs F02_01 (>SMA10); F02_10 (10/30 exit, 20/50 re-entry) vs F01_02 (10/30 both); F02_06 (3-day confirmed re-entry above SMA50) vs F01_06-style symmetric filter. Sign tests across assets
evidence: F02_02 vs F02_01: Sharpe better on 44% (median -0.019), drawdown better on 72%; F02_10 vs F01_02: Sharpe better on 31% (median -0.042), drawdown better on 81%; F02_06 vs F01_06: Sharpe better on 16% (median -0.066), drawdown better on 69%

claim: Semiconductor strategies benefit disproportionately from momentum during sustained industry expansion
test: Momentum family (F03) Sharpe minus buy-and-hold Sharpe, semis vs broad ETFs (Mann-Whitney); and momentum excess return vs buy-and-hold inside ex-ante 'up' trend regimes
evidence: Momentum Sharpe minus B&H: semis -0.113 (n=14), broad -0.121 (n=7), diff +0.008, p=0.856. In up-trend regimes momentum excess vs B&H: semis -6.11%/yr, broad -2.43%/yr (negative = momentum lags holding during expansions)

claim: Mean reversion performs better in sideways regimes than in strong directional trends
test: For each mean-reversion strategy x asset: Sharpe in ex-ante sideways regime minus average Sharpe in up/down regimes; sign test across assets
evidence: Sideways minus trend-regime Sharpe: median -0.164; positive for 25% of 32 assets (p=0.007); excess return vs B&H sideways minus trend: median +2.61%/yr

claim: Sector-specific strategy selection outperforms one common signal for all sectors, after model-selection bias
test: Walk-forward: each fold picks the best IS strategy per sector vs the strategy with the best mean IS Sharpe across sectors; compare OOS Sharpe (t-test on fold means)
evidence: OOS Sharpe specific minus common: mean -0.205 over 196 sector-folds (37% positive); fold-mean t-test p=0.045. Specific-selection IS->OOS Sharpe decay +0.66

claim: Performance deteriorates materially once transaction costs and slippage are included
test: Re-run every strategy x asset at 0/5/10/20/50 bps. 'Material' (pre-specified) = median Sharpe drop >= 0.10 from 0 to 10 bps, or >= 25% relative fall in the share of combinations beating buy-and-hold
evidence: 0 bps: median Sharpe 0.37, 24% beat B&H; 5 bps: median Sharpe 0.33, 20% beat B&H; 10 bps: median Sharpe 0.30, 16% beat B&H; 20 bps: median Sharpe 0.24, 11% beat B&H; 50 bps: median Sharpe 0.09, 6% beat B&H. Median Sharpe drop 0->10 bps 0.048; 90th pct 0.163

claim: Many top-ranked in-sample strategies fail to retain their ranking out of sample
test: Per asset and fold: Spearman(IS Sharpe rank, next-year OOS Sharpe rank); share of IS top-decile strategies still top-decile OOS. Supported if retention < 50% and fewer than 75% stay in the upper half
evidence: Mean Spearman +0.119 over 657 asset-folds; top-decile retention 12% vs chance 10% (t-test vs chance p=0.000); 58% of IS top-decile land in the OOS upper half; best-IS strategy's median OOS percentile 58%

claim: Some apparent advantages disappear after matching invested exposure or volatility
test: Among strategy x asset combinations with a shallower drawdown than buy-and-hold, share that also beat a static asset/cash mix with the same volatility (CAGR and drawdown). Supported if fewer than half retain both
evidence: 2702 of 2911 combos have shallower drawdowns than B&H; vs the volatility-matched mix 15% have higher CAGR, 58% shallower drawdown, 14% both. Of 188 combos beating B&H CAGR, 99% also beat the exposure-matched mix

claim: Combining complementary signals produces greater robustness than optimising a single indicator
test: Hybrid family (F10) vs the median of the nine single-idea families on four robustness measures: share of assets with Sharpe above B&H, cross-asset dispersion, IS->OOS Sharpe decay, parameter sensitivity. Supported if better on >=3 of 4
evidence: share_pos_sharpe_diff: hybrids 0.209 vs median single-family 0.156 (better); disp_sharpe_diff: hybrids 0.203 vs median single-family 0.167 (worse); median_is_oos_decay: hybrids 0.026 vs median single-family -0.028 (worse); median_param_sharpe_std: hybrids 0.063 vs median single-family 0.059 (worse). Ensemble F10_07 beats B&H Sharpe on 16% of assets
